Grand Master Charvonia’s Recommendation No. 10
Updates Ritual and Ceremonies to Use the Term “Holy Writings”
When Describing the Volume of the Sacred Law
Freemasonry is inclusive of the faiths of all of its members. Our Ritual
and ceremonies are meant to reflect this inclusiveness. For example, the Ritual uses
the term “Great Architect of the Universe” to refer to the Divine so that Brothers of
different faiths may participate in prayers together. As another example, men may
be obligated on the Holy Writings of their respective faiths. The language used
within our Ritual and ceremonies can better reflect Freemasonry’s inclusiveness
so that the various religions and faiths of the men who join our Craft are
treated equally.

demonstrating the inclusiveness of all books of faith of the Craft’s members.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The Entered Apprentice Degree teaches that Freemasonry unites men of
all religions and sects. To accommodate applicants and brothers of various faiths,
the California Masonic Code authorizes the use of a variety of Holy Writings
during the conferring of degrees. However, when a Holy Writing other than a Holy
Bible is used during a degree or ceremony, it is referred to as either a Bible, Holy
Bible, or the Holy Scriptures. This practice may confuse and offend candidates
of other faiths. This recommendation is intended to mitigate such confusion
and offense.
This recommendation seeks to replace the terms “Bible,” “Holy Bible,”
and “Holy Scriptures” with the term “Holy Writings” in our Ritual and ceremonies,
except where there are specific references to the Holy Bible, such as the Book of
Genesis. The Grand Secretary and Ritual Committee would be authorized to make
the changes to the Ritual and ceremonies. Changes to the Monitor and Officers
Manual are indicated in the recommendation. Printed documents, like the cipher,
would be amended during the next manufacturing order.

not reflect changes made to the Ritual. It will be the responsibility of District
Inspectors and Officers Coaches to ensure timely adoption of the changes without
new ciphers.

Resolution No. 14-01
Clarifies the Grand Master’s Right to Review a Trial Dismissal
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify the Grand Master’s
right to review and reinstate a trial dismissal.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section 1404.315 of the California Masonic Code allows
the Committee on Jurisprudence to dismiss charges of unmasonic conduct, if in
the judgment of the Committee all of the facts set forth in the charges, if true,
would not warrant a guilty verdict; and
WHEREAS, this power allows the dismissal of unwarranted charges
without the expense and embarrassment of a trial; and
WHEREAS, it would be helpful to clarify the Grand Master’s power to
review a dismissal.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 1404.315 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.315. REVIEW OF THE CHARGES BY THE COMMITTEE
ON JURISPRUDENCE.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
In 2010, the portion of the California Masonic Code that dealt with
Masonic trials was rewritten and approved. Under Section 1404.315 of the new
provisions, the Committee on Jurisprudence was charged with the responsibility
of reviewing all charges for potential Masonic trials at the time that the charges
were submitted to Grand Lodge. The Committee on Jurisprudence was authorized
to remove those charges of unmasonic conduct for which the evidence was not
adequate as well as to revise any portions of the charges that were incorrect,
ambiguous, or insufficient. The Committee on Jurisprudence can also dismiss any
charges which it believed that, even if the facts were all true, would not result in a
finding of unmasonic conduct. This was all intended to identify frivolous charges
at the outset and save the time, expense, and embarrassment of futile trials.

The Committee on Jurisprudence shall review all charges and
specifications received by the Grand Secretary, strike out those portions of any
charge which are not supported by a clear and precise specification of unmasonic
conduct and revise those portions of any charge which are incorrect, ambiguous
or insufficient, based on the specifications. The committee may work with the
Accuser during its review. The committee shall append to the charge or charges
a statement setting forth the portion or portions of Section 1401.010 under which
each charge is being brought and every essential factual element of the unmasonic
conduct specified which must be proven at trial in order for the Accused to be found
guilty of that specification. After its review, the Committee on Jurisprudence shall
provide the Grand Secretary with the charge or charges as they may have been
revised by the committee. The Grand Secretary shall provide the Grand Master
with a copy of the charge or charges as revised by the committee upon receipt.

A copy of the Committee on Jurisprudence’s findings is forwarded to
the Grand Secretary and then to the Grand Master. As is stated in CMC section
404.130 A, the Grand Master has supervisory capacity over the craft and, as such,
it has always been his province to overrule the findings of any committee. Thus,
he always has had the power to reinstitute charges. However, this explicit wording
is not contained in the current section 1404.315. The proponents of Resolution
14-01 seek to add such wording.

If in the judgment of the Committee on Jurisprudence all of the facts
set forth in any of the charges and specifications, if true, would not warrant a
verdict of unmasonic conduct, then any such charge shall be dismissed by it and
the committee shall so advise the Grand Secretary. Such a dismissal shall not
prevent any subsequent filing of a charge with more evidence. The Committee
on Jurisprudence shall prepare a written report on its action and file it with the

At the 165th Annual Communication, when this resolution was first
considered, your Committee on Trial Review reported as follows:

This proposal simply explicitly states what has always been implicitly
recognized. It does not change how any Masonic trial will be conducted in the
future or how it will be subsequently reviewed.
Report from the Trial Review Committee

Resolution 14-01 seeks to clarify the Grand Master’s power to reinstate
Masonic charges dismissed by the Jurisprudence Committee.

206

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

The current procedure is that when charges are filed against a Mason
they are initially sent to the Jurisprudence Committee which reviews the form
of the charges and makes a determination of whether or not they state a Masonic
offense, more specifically they determine that if all of the facts alleged in the
charges are true whether or not they would constitute a Masonic offense. This
process is integral to our purpose because it allows for the weeding out of frivolous
charges and charges which can never result in a conviction, thus saving the grand
lodge and the constituent lodges substantial time and money, and saving those
involved the embarrassment and humiliation of having to go through a trial which
is destined to lead nowhere.

Resolution No. 14-05
Creates Rules Governing Cemetery Property

The Code already requires that when Jurisprudence determines that
charges should be dismissed it shall notify the Grand Secretary and prepare a
report as to the reasons for the dismissal and that that report shall be forwarded to
the Grand Master. CMC §404.130(a) gives the Grand Master general supervisory
power over Grand Lodge during its recess. It can be argued that that power
includes the power to reverse dismissals ordered by the Jurisprudence Committee.
This resolution seeks to clarify that and to specifically establish that the Grand
Master does have the power to reinstate charges after dismissal by Jurisprudence.
It therefore only seeks to clarify that the Grand Master has that power. It does not
give him the power to reverse a decision of Grand Lodge. If the case is reinstated
it will proceed to trial and the result will ultimately be reviewed by the Committee
on Trial Review and voted on by Grand Lodge. This resolution does not
change that.
While it is true that not all Grand Masters are lawyers the function of
the Jurisprudence Committee is designed to guide the Grand Master on the legal
complexities involved in a particular case. Additionally, our law provides that
the Grand Master shall have the ultimate authority over the workings of Grand
Lodge while it is in recess and it would be inconsistent with that power to allow a
Committee to make a decision which he cannot reverse.
As the Grand Master probably already has the power to do what the
resolution seeks to accomplish it is prudent to spell it out in the Code.
For the reasons stated, the Committee is of the opinion that this
clarification of the Code is constructive and well taken and therefore recommends
a yes vote on the resolution.
One member of the Committee recused himself from the vote on this
resolution because he is one of the proponents of the resolution.
The Committee on Trial Review adopts the 2014 report and again
recommends a yes vote on Resolution 14-01.
One member has again recused himself from voting since he is one of the
proponents of the resolution.
Resolution APPROVED.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 809.130 of the California Masonic

§809.130. LODGE INVESTMENTS.
Exclusive of a Lodge investment in an incorporated Masonic Hall
Association, Masonic cemetery property or any Lodge revolving funds, a Lodge
may invest its funds only as provided in this section. The Lodge’s investments
allowed under this section (other than cash, cash equivalents, checking accounts,
savings accounts and certificates of deposit) shall be administered either by an
investment committee appointed by the Master or by trustees as provided in
Section 809.110 of this Code. No investment committee or trustee administration
shall be required for the Lodge’s cash, cash equivalents, checking accounts,
savings accounts or certificates of deposit.
Lodge funds shall be invested with the care, skill, prudence and diligence
under the circumstances then prevailing, including, but not limited to, the general
economic conditions and the anticipated needs of the Lodge, that a prudent person
acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in the conduct
of an enterprise of like character and with like aims to accomplish the purposes
of the Lodge.
Through the Lodge investment committee or trustees, the Lodge shall
confer and counsel as to any proposed or contemplated investments under this
section with a Registered Investment Advisor of its choice. A Lodge may freely
choose to accept or reject any and all recommendations made to it by the Advisor.
Alternatively, a Lodge may retain a Registered Investment Advisor operating as
an investment manager who offers standardized portfolios through a managed
investment account.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
Over the past several years, Lodges throughout this jurisdiction have
become recipients of cemetery property. A committee was formed in 2012 to
standardize cemetery property management and the results of its deliberations
led to a number of proposed resolutions that were submitted for the 2013
Annual Communication.
Resolution 13-22 did not achieve a majority vote and was defeated in
2013. The intent of that resolution was to provide the details of how lodges could
acquire cemetery property. However, in order to prevent lodges from speculating
in such property, a number of complicated restrictions were part of that
resolution. The proponents introduced Resolution 14-05, which removes much of
this language.
Under this resolution, Lodges would be required to report to the Grand Secretary
information regarding cemetery property. The Grand Secretary would then create
and maintain a database of all cemetery property owned by Lodges throughout
the state.
This resolution would also require Grand Lodge approval for a Lodge to
expend more than $15,000 a year in cemetery property purchases. Lodges would
specifically be authorized to accept donations of cemetery property without limit.

212

213

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

However, all cemetery property must be in the name of the Lodge and not any
other person or body, including a Hall Association. This is consistent with 2014
Grand Master Decision Number 2, which indicates that a Hall Association may
not own cemetery property.

WHEREAS, the Memorial was constructed in the 1920’s with strong
support and leadership from the Grand Lodge of California; and

This proposal states that a Lodge may use cemetery property for interring
eligible Masons and adds a new class of eligible Masonic relatives. The Lodge
may also sell the property to any person at its discretion, with the proceeds being
placed in its general funds.
Challenges in implementation may arise from poor record keeping.
Some Lodges may not have documentation showing ownership of all cemetery
properties purchased or donated in the distant past. Furthermore, some Masonic
Cemetery Property may still be held by Hall Associations or some other persons
or bodies.
Section 809.140A.4 states that real property should be owned by
Masonic Hall Associations. However, future interment rights are not viewed as
real property, but rather as intangible personal property.
Of particular concern, rulings of the Internal Revenue Service suggest
that holding cemeteries or burial plots is not consistent with the tax-exempt
status of our Hall Associations. Thus, concern about losing our nonprofit status
dictates that the prudent course for the ownership of such property is in the
name of a Lodge and not a Masonic Hall Association. While there may be some
inconvenience from the transferring of these properties from Hall Associations to
Lodges the important benefit of retaining our nonprofit status outweighs any of
these inconveniences.

WHEREAS, the Memorial has become an important destination for
Masons as well as the general public; and
WHEREAS, the Memorial operates with the financial support of
American Masons whose unified support perpetuates this symbol of veneration
for our first and greatest president; and
WHEREAS, approximately half of the Grand Lodges in the United
States have adopted resolutions to provide annual contributions to the
Memorial of at least $1 per year per Mason, many are in addition to candidate
contributions; and
WHEREAS, the Masons of California are proud of our past support and
leadership of the Memorial and wish to help ensure its future.

§407.025. PER CAPITA LODGE CONTRIBUTIONS.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents of this Resolution seek to provide a permanent per capita
assessment of $1.00 per Mason for the support of the George Washington Masonic
National Memorial thereby helping to ensure its future.
On February 22, 1910, representatives from twenty-six Grand Lodges
met in Alexandria Virginia to form an association to build a memorial to George
Washington. Ten years later, the concept of a colossal building to honor Washington
was approved by the Grand Lodges of the United States. The groundbreaking
took place on June 5, 1922. The Memorial Association was determined to not
borrow any money for the construction of the building. So, construction was only
able to continue as funds were available.

On November 1, 1923, the Memorial’s cornerstone was dedicated by
President Calvin Coolidge and Former President William Taft to a crowd of
thousands. Finally, on May 12, 1932, the Memorial was dedicated. From the
initial meeting in 1910 until the dedication in 1932, California Masons donated
over $755,000 for the construction of this Memorial.
This resolution will amend Section 407.025 of the California Masonic
Code by requiring each Mason carried on the rolls as of June 30th, to pay a per
capita sum of $1.00 for the support of the George Washington Masonic National
Memorial. This section of the CMC already provides for other types of per
capita assessments.
The First Degree teaches us the importance of charity. There are currently
26 Grand Lodges contributing $1 per member. California has the opportunity
to continue its long tradition of supporting the George Washington Masonic
National Memorial.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents of Resolution 2014-14 seek to add a Grand Historian
as an additional Grand Lodge Officer and specify the duties this Officer must
perform. This Resolution would also require the Grand Lecturer, with the approval
of the Grand Master, to make the appropriate changes to applicable Grand
Lodge Ceremonies.
The Grand Lodge of California has existed for many years without a
Grand Historian; however the Grand Lodge staff has endeavored to accomplish
the preservation of historical artifacts throughout our Jurisdiction along with
managing our museum at the Grand Lodge building. Grand Lodge, through the
Institute for Masonic Studies, governs the Henry Wilson Coil Masonic Library
and Museum. It will be necessary to deconflict the duties of the Grand Historian
and Grand Lodge staff to avoid duplication of effort. If each incoming Grand
Master appoints a different Grand Historian, historical preservation efforts may
lack consistency and be disrupted from year to year.
The duties of the Grand Historian will necessitate travel throughout the
state, which will be an additional expense for Grand Lodge. The Committee on
Finance has reported that this legislation would add expenses to the Grand Lodge
Budget in the range of $6,500 to $10,000 per year.
However, it is within the purview of Grand Lodge to decide how best
to accomplish historical preservation, whether through a Grand Lodge officer,
Grand Lodge staff, or the efforts of individual lodges.
There are challenges in implementing this resolution. After the conclusion
of this Annual Communication, the incoming Grand Master shall appoint a Grand
Historian to serve through the next Annual Communication. It 212 Proceedings
of the Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California 213 would be necessary to amend the
Grand Master’s budget to include the expenses of the Grand Historian, including
travel and the purchasing of regalia. The Grand Lecturer, with the approval of the
Grand Master, would modify the ritual of the applicable Grand Lodge ceremonies
as required to include the Grand Historian. The participation of the Grand
Historian in Grand Lodge ceremonies may be limited until regalia are available
and rituals modified.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

217

Report from the Finance Committee
The proponents of this resolution seek to add the Grand Lodge Officer
position of Grand Historian. The Resolution requires the Grand Historian to assist
in the preservation of artifacts held by Grand Lodge, to travel through the state
to assist individual lodges in researching the lodge history and preserving lodge
artifacts. The Grand Historian is further obligated to write scholarly articles for
publication and perform other duties that might be assigned by the Grand Master.
Section 407.070 of the California Masonic Code requires the Grand
Lodge reimburse Grand Lodge Officers for their necessary, out of pocket expenses
in the performance of their duties. The Resolution does not mandate the amount
of travel the Grand Historian should undertake. This would likely be a decision
of the Grand Master who will have planned for such expenses as Deputy Grand
Master. In addition there will be initial costs of regalia and other items regularly
provided to all Grand Lodge Officers.
It is therefore the opinion of the Committee on Finance that this
Resolution, if adopted, would add expenses to the Grand Lodge Budget in the
range of $6,000 to $9,000 per year.
Resolution FAILED.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
Supporters of this resolution seek to allow for an online Candidate
Learning Center for the convenience of lodges and their members and also to
ensure a quality Masonic education for new candidates. If adopted, this resolution
will amend Section 804.620 of the California Masonic Code to allow utilization of
the Candidate Learning Center, which has already been developed. The candidate
and lodges still have the option of traditional basic Masonic education as before
(outlined in Section 804.620), but the Candidate Learning Center will serve as
an alternative.
Candidates will have 24-hour access to necessary Masonic education,
convenient to their schedules. The Candidate Learning Center will provide the
option of a standardized candidate education throughout California Freemasonry.
The Candidate Learning Center can also track results and report progress to
the lodges.
Being a dynamic program, the contents of the subject matter may be
changed from time to time when deemed appropriate by the Grand Master. The
Candidate Learning Center does not replace the oral examination in his proficiency
in a tiled lodge. It provides an alternative to the written questions from the Basic
Masonic Education course pamphlets.
It is the choice of the Candidate whether to use the Candidate Learning
Center or to use the traditional written materials. Should the candidate choose the
Candidate Learning Center, it is the choice of the Lodge either to pay or require
the candidate to pay.
As the world increases access to on-line information, allowing the option
of the Candidate Learning Center would align California Masonic education more
closely with the expectations of new members.
Resolution APPROVED.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents seek to create the procedure for Lodge approval of the
sale of buildings.
Section 406.060.E of the California Masonic Code on Masonic Properties
includes the requirement for the approval by the Committee on Masonic Properties
for “any option or contract regarding the sale or listing for sale of real property.”
The Masonic Properties Committee also provides a form and checklist for the sale
of property for use by a Hall Association. However, no procedure of how to obtain
the approval is provided.
The California Corporations Code requires Lodge consent before a
Masonic Hall Association may sell its building but our California Masonic Code
does not specify how that consent will be obtained. A review of the Ross Digest of
1949 and the California Masonic Code, including supplements, of 1956 and 1975
did not address this issue.
This resolution creates the procedure for Lodges to approve the
disposition of real property and will satisfy the requirements of the California
Corporations Code. It would provide additional safeguards to Lodge members by
requiring advance notification of any sale, as well as approval by the Lodge and
Grand Lodge. If multiple Lodges are shareholders in a building, then each Lodge
must approve the sale.

§809.130. LODGE INVESTMENTS.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents of this resolution seek to make it an option for Lodges
to have their investment funds invested by the Grand Lodge. This resolution is
similar to Resolution 12-08 which was approved and gave Lodges the ability to

232

233

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

invest their Life Membership funds through Grand Lodge. This legislation would
also add administration of the Grand Lodge Life Membership fund as a duty of
the Grand Treasurer.

The committee finds the resolution to be favorable for lodges and notes
the following advantages:

The investment industry is highly specialized and many, if not most,
Lodges don’t have members or resources to properly manage their investment
portfolios. Often, they choose brothers with little to no knowledge of investing
to make decisions on their Lodges complicated and important investments.
Lodge Trustees have a fiduciary responsibility to the Lodge. Investing in safe,
low earning investments can be breach of that responsibility just the same as
investing in highly risky investments. The option to invest their money through
Grand Lodge would give Lodges the ability to enlist the help of the same trained
professionals that have been successfully managing our Grand Lodges interests
for years. In addition, by pooling monies into a trust, there may be more options
available than a Lodge would have on its own.
It should be noted however, that Grand Lodge would not provide daily
investment results. These results would likely be available on a quarterly basis.
If a Lodge wants to monitor its portfolio more frequently, then this option might
not be right for them.
To opt-in to this program a Lodge would have to vote by a 2/3 majority
after advance notice was given to all members. To terminate the program however,
it takes a simple majority vote of members present at any Stated Meeting.
This program would be optional and thus, if a Lodge is comfortable in
managing its investments, would not apply. But for those Lodges that don’t have
investment savvy members, it would give them additional resources to make sure
they are investing their money wisely.
Report from the Investment Committee
A few years ago, Resolution 12-08 was presented and subsequently
adopted which gave lodges the option to request that grand lodge help
administer their life membership funds. Three years later, Resolution 15-02 is
now being presented to give lodges the option of requesting help from grand
lodge to administer their general lodge funds. This resolution simply expands
the investment services available to lodges from just life membership to any and
all of the lodge investments…solely at the discretion of the lodge. It is by no
means a solicitation nor requirement that lodges participate. And the lodge has
full discretion over which investments they would like grand lodge to assist with.
As in Resolution 12-08, the Grand Treasurer’s duties would be amended
to oversee the investment program administering lodge investments. The lodge
would act upon the recommendation of either the lodge’s board of trustees or
the lodge’s investment committee. And, it would require a 2/3 vote by the lodge
members at a stated meeting (as outlined in the Resolution).

• Diversification
• Ease of burden
1) Diversification: Grand Lodge currently uses a third party money
manager to oversee funds invested for the Masonic Homes, the California
Masonic Foundation, and lodges’ life membership funds (for those has
that have chosen to participate). They have a highly diversified line up of
mutual funds which are monitored and adjusted on a regular basis.
2) Ease of Burden: Lodges that choose to have Grand Lodge invest their
investment assets would eliminate the administrative burden of (1st)
choosing the investments (2nd) monitoring the performance.
This Resolution does not relinquish power or control of lodge
investment funds to Grand Lodge. It simply allows a lodge to retain Grand
Lodge to invest and administer its investment assets on behalf of the Lodge. This
arrangement can be terminated at any time by majority vote of the lodge members
at stated meeting. The Committee on Investments supports the adoption of
resolution 15-02.

in order to replace dues income; and

plan from the payment of dues in the Lodge. The resolution may be adopted,
amended or revoked at any Stated Meeting by a majority vote of the members
present. Any such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated
Meeting and written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the
text of the proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is
to be taken. The plan must provide that a life membership shall be granted upon
payment of:

The Grand Secretary shall provide the form of contract to be used by the
Lodge when a life membership is purchased (other than as a memorial). Such
contract must be signed by the member for whom the life membership is being
purchased, the Lodge Master and the Lodge Secretary, affixed with the seal of the
Lodge. The original shall be kept as part of the member’s permanent membership
record. A copy of the signed contract shall be provided to the member.

A.

A sum of money which is not less equal to or greater than 20.83 22 times
the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase of the life membership;
or

A life member who has been suspended or expelled and who shall
thereafter become restored or elected to membership in a Lodge in which a life
membership was once held shall also be restored as a life member of that Lodge.

B.

A sum of money equal to the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase
of the life membership multiplied by the factor indicated opposite the
member’s age in the following schedule:

Age 49 and under, 21 a factor equal to or greater than 24
times annual dues;
50 to 54 inclusive, 19 a factor equal to or greater than 20

The Secretary shall send to each life member at his last known address,
annually, a Life Membership Dues Card for the next calendar year.
A life membership is an executed contract. A life member has no interest
in the Lodge’s Life Membership Fund, except in the case of a rescission of his
life membership with his consent and the consent of the Lodge or as elsewhere
provided in this Code.

The proponents of this resolution seek to amend Section 809.320 of the
California Masonic Code to modify the formula for determining the amount of
money required to purchase a life membership.
If adopted, this legislation would modify the two formulas available for
determining the cost of a life membership. The fixed price formula would increase
from 20.83 to 22 times annual dues, and the variable formula would increase
across all age categories. In addition, the 65 and over category would be split into
two categories: 65 to 71 and 72 and over.
Similar legislation was introduced in 2013 as Resolution 2013-12, which
also increased the cost multiplier. It was carried over to 2014 but not adopted by
Grand Lodge.

236

237

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

This graph compares the life membership dues multiplier as a function of
age for the current plan, the previous legislation 13-12, and the proposal currently
under consideration (2015-03).

It can be seen that 13-12 and 15-03 provide comparable increases in the
dues multiplier up to age 50. After age 50, 15-03 provides a lower dues multiplier
compared to the previous proposal 13-12. Compared to the current method, 15-03
provides the greatest increase for ages 20 to 50 and 65 to 71.
A life membership is intended to be a mutually beneficial arrangement
between a member and his Lodge. The member avoids future dues increases,
gains the convenience of never having to pay dues again and the assurance of
never being suspended for non-payment of dues, regardless of his future financial
condition. The Lodge gains a sum of money that can be invested to produce a
revenue stream in perpetuity. It is incumbent upon the Lodge to invest this sum to
gain a rate of return sufficient to compensate for the loss of future dues payments.
The fair price of a life membership is a function of life expectancy,
inflation (as reflected in future dues increases), and the expected rate of return
over the member’s lifetime. The current pricing formula was determined years
ago during a period when life expectancy was lower and conservative investments
produced a higher rate of return than today.
One consequence of this legislation may be that fewer life memberships
are purchased due to the increase in cost. However, a life membership that is
underpriced is a financial burden for a Lodge.
This legislation would not affect the amount of money received by a
life member who, with the consent of the Lodge, rescinds his life membership as
provided in Section 809.320 of the CMC.
This resolution would be implemented by the Grand Secretary’s office.
Report from the Investment Committee
In 2013, a similar resolution was presented, Resolution 13-12. That
resolution was carried-over to 2014 but did not pass. Resolution 13-12, like 1503 now before us, sought a change in the multipliers used to calculate the sum
of a lifetime membership in our lodges. The argument being that a lodge loses
current revenue (in the form of an annual dues payment from a lodge member)
in favor of (1) relieving a brother from making further annual dues payments and
(2) building a lodge reserve fund that will be invested for long-term growth, and
which will provide a recurring smaller revenue stream of the interest or returns
earned from that investment fund. In order to help a lodge replace the near-term
lost income from a dues payment, new multipliers have been proposed to increase
the sum required to purchase a lifetime membership…thereby increasing the size
of the life membership fund, which in turn will produce a higher interest or return
amount from that investment pool when withdrawn annually.

older members of our lodges was too high. 15-03 has proposed a new multiplier
table and added an additional age bracket to specifically address the concern that
we provide a funding level that is more favorable for older members.

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify the provisions that
permit a Master Mason to be the Master, Warden or Secretary of a Research Lodge
at the same time as he is Master, Warden or Secretary of a Constituent lodge, as
well as create a similar provision applicable to Historic Lodges.
In 2006 Grand Lodge modified CMC Section 804.120 to allow a Master
Mason to be the Master, Warden or Secretary of a Research Lodge at the same
time as he is Master, Warden or Secretary of a Constituent lodge. Historic Lodges
are modeled after Research Lodges.
This Resolution would modify CMC Section 805.010 to add a limited
exemption to the prohibition of a member from serving as Master, Warden or
Secretary of more than one lodge at the same time.
This resolution also will amend section 814.000 (Research Lodges) of
the California Masonic Code, adding the following statement: “A member may
be the Master, a Warden, or the Secretary of a Research Lodge at the same time
as he is the Master, a Warden, or the Secretary of one or more other Lodges.”
This resolution will also add the following statement to section 816.000 (Historic
236 Proceedings of the Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California 237 Lodges) of
the California Masonic Code: “A member may be the Master, a Warden, or the
Secretary of a Historic Lodge at the same time as he is the Master, a Warden, or
the Secretary of one or more other Lodges.”
If adopted, this resolution will permit a Master Mason serving as Master,
a Warden, or the Secretary of a Constituent Lodge to simultaneously serve as
Master, a Warden, or Secretary of one or more Research Lodges and/or one or
more Historic Lodges. Such multiple tenures do not pose any conflict of interest
injurious to Freemasonry but will increase the pool of prospective leaders for
Research and Historic Lodges.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

WHEREAS, before the adoption of Grand Master Nagel’s
Recommendation No. 3, which substantially reformed our Masonic trial
procedures, a suspended Mason could be restored by the Lodge which suspended
him; and
WHEREAS, the suspended Master Mason who was a member of more
than one Lodge was only required to petition the Lodge which suspended him and
no others; and
WHEREAS, the legislation adopted as a result of Grand Master Nagel’s
Recommendation No. 3 changed this rule and now requires such a suspended
Master Mason to petition and be restored by every one of the Lodges of which he
was a member at the time of his suspension; and
WHEREAS, this new rule has placed a burden on suspended Master
Masons with multiple memberships that was not imposed before the adoption of
Grand Master Nagel’s Recommendation No. 3; and
WHEREAS, the proponents believe that it would be fair and appropriate
to allow each Lodge to make its own decision on whether to restore a suspended
Master Mason to membership; and
WHEREAS, the proponents were actively involved in the preparation
and presentation of Grand Master Nagel’s Recommendation No. 3.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 1404.1000 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.1000. RESTORATION OF A SUSPENDED MASON.
A.

A Mason suspended for a definite period as a result of any charge of
unmasonic conduct filed in this Jurisdiction shall be restored to the rights
and privileges of Masonry upon the last to occur of (a) the expiration
of the term of his suspension and (b) the payment of any dues and the
performance of any other obligations required for his restoration in
this Jurisdiction.

B.

A Mason suspended for an indefinite period as a result of any charge of
unmasonic conduct filed in this Jurisdiction may be restored to the rights
and privileges of Masonry as follows:

Report from the Legislative Analysis Committee
The proponents of resolution 15-05 seek to change the California
Masonic Code so that a Mason who was a member of more than one lodge and
who has been indefinitely suspended as a result of a Masonic trial can have his
membership restored in a particular lodge by an action of that particular lodge.
If a Mason is found to be guilty of unmasonic conduct, one of three
punishments can be imposed, namely a reprimand in open lodge, a suspension
for some degree of time, or lifetime expulsion. The choice of punishment reflects
the severity of the misconduct. At the extreme, such as an act of moral turpitude,
expulsion is the consequence. Typically suspension is imposed for some
intermediate, and often local, misbehavior that occurs in one lodge or between
particular Masons. Prior to 2006, all penalties for suspension were indefinite and
a restoration to membership could only be accomplished by an action of the lodge
that suspended him or by Grand Lodge.

250

251

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

These conditions for restoration were incorporated into the 2006 version
of the CMC. In 2009, the CMC was amended to introduce two types of suspension,
namely one that was for a fixed period of time and the other for suspension for
an indefinite amount of time. In 2010, the entire code section on Masonic trials
was rewritten and adopted as Grand Master Nagel’s Recommendation Number 3.
In this version, the wording of section 1404.1000 B 1 was rewritten to state that
actions to annul an indefinite suspension were to occur in the “Mason’s lodge”
rather than “the lodge that suspended him”. Since a man who is suspended by
one lodge is automatically suspended by all of the lodges to which he belongs,
all of those lodges in which he had held membership would have to agree to the
removal of the suspension or Grand Lodge would have to remove it.

The reason for seeking the proposed solution is not described in the
resolution. One possible explanation may be that a Mason might be suspended
by a lodge in which there is residual animosity that would prevent the suspended
Mason from getting a fair vote. It was not the intent of our law to allow suspensions
to turn into de facto expulsions. However, in such cases, the suspended Mason
could still apply to Grand Lodge for restoration.

The proponents wish to simplify the restoration process when a man is
a member of multiple lodges by only requiring one lodge to restore a suspended
Mason. However, those providing the restoration would not necessarily be either
the lodge or the Masons who were initially wronged.
Currently a suspension, either for unmasonic conduct or for non-payment
of dues, cannot be reversed until all of the lodges to which the man belonged
agree. In the case of suspension for non-payment of dues, all lodges to which he
was in arrears have to be paid. In the event that Grand Lodge restores a man who
was suspended for unmasonic conduct, there is specific language in the CMC
indicating that such a person becomes “unaffiliated” and is no longer suspended,
although he must then apply for membership in a lodge. However, unaffiliated
status can only be granted by Grand Lodge, so no such language exists in the
current proposal.
Thus the resolution creates a unique situation in Masonry in California,
namely one in which a man could be a member of one lodge and yet be suspended
by another lodge. The precise status of this man in Masonry in California is not
defined. For example, what if this man became an officer in the lodge that voted
to remove the suspension, but both this lodge and a lodge that had not voted to
restore him were in the same inspectorial district? Would this man be allowed
to attend a school of instruction? What would be the man’s status if he chose to
apply to a new lodge of which he had never been a member? Would such a man
be entitled to attend Grand Lodge? It also seems illogical to require automatic
suspension in all lodges in which a man is a member when suspension is imposed
but then permit restoration by only one of those lodges. The adoption of this
resolution would bring significant confusion.
Since the intent of the resolution is to allow the restoration process to be
undertaken by a single lodge, a proposal could have been made to return to our
previous practice of having restoration done by the lodge that initially suspended
the man. In this way, the man would have to demonstrate to those parties that
rehabilitation and contrition had occurred. Alternatively, one could propose
a revision to the law that would set a maximum time limit for an indefinite
suspension, after which time the man could then be granted unaffiliated status.

In conclusion, this resolution is making a change that will create
confusion in the Jurisdiction and may be doing so to solve a problem for which
other, and simpler, solutions exist.
Report from the Trial Review Committee
The California Masonic Code in section 1404.1000 B 3 specifically
states: “If the suspended Mason was a member of more than one Constituent
Lodge when he was suspended, he may not be restored without the consent of
each such Lodge, if it is not dissolved.”
Resolution 15-05 seeks to change the requirement of consent by each
Constituent Lodge of which the Mason is a member to permit restoration by
consent of one such Lodge, and further states “restoration by one Lodge shall
not restore him to membership in any other Lodge without the consent of such
other Lodge.”
On the surface this Resolution appears fair; however, the resolution fails
to take into account that without appropriate modification of California Masonic
Code section 809.165(A) there is a conflict in the brother’s status. Since he was
suspended, albeit by operation of the trial provisions of our Masonic Code found
in Chapter 14, the proponents seek to allow a multiple member to regain active
status by a vote of a single lodge. By the terms of the amendment he is still
suspended from membership in any lodge that does not vote to readmit him he
therefore remains “suspended.” Section 804.165(A) states, in part “…suspension
or expulsion of a multiple member in this Jurisdiction shall automatically suspend
his membership or expel him from membership in all Constituent Lodges.” That
same section also states “Such reinstatement shall automatically restore him to
membership in every other Constituent Lodge of which he was a member, upon
payment of any dues and the performance of any other obligations required for his
restoration to membership in this Jurisdiction.”
All a suspend brother need do is pay his dues. He does not have to
perform “… any other obligations required for his restoration to membership in
this Jurisdiction.” The proposed resolution calls for consent which conflicts with
section 804.165 A of the Code. An obligation is a condition of being morally
or legally bound to do something. The proposed resolution requires that a lodge
must vote on readmission. That is not an obligation of the brother; it is a right
granted by the proposed resolution to “any other lodge” from which the brother
was suspended.

252

Proceedings of the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

If the code were thus amended it could be argued that after a reinstatement
by one lodge all a brother would have to do is pay dues to the other. It also
appears that a brother could be a readmitted to membership in one lodge and
still suspended in another which leave unanswered what is his status should he
seek to join or visit a third lodge or be active in or join a body which requires
Masonic membership in good standing as a condition of membership. Is he in
good standing or is he a suspended Mason?

Resolution No. 15-06
Cleans Up and Clarifies Portions of the California Masonic Code
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clean up and clarify portions
of the California Masonic Code.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Fourth Edition of the California Masonic Code became
effective at the close of the 2006 Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge on
October 11, 2006; and
WHEREAS, since then, users of the Fourth Edition have identified a
number of places where the language of the Fourth Edition should be cleaned-up
or clarified; and
WHEREAS, this resolution addresses those places found since the
adoption of Resolution 13-15.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 20.000 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§20.000. MEMBERS.
A.

Grand Lodge shall be composed of a Grand Master (whose manner of
address shall be Most Worshipful), a Deputy Grand Master, a Senior
Grand Warden, and a Junior Grand Warden (whose manner of address
shall be Right Worshipful), a Grand Treasurer, a Grand Secretary and a
Grand Lecturer (whose manner of address shall be Very Worshipful), a
Grand Chaplain (whose manner of address shall be Very Reverend), the
Assistant Grand Lecturers, a Grand Orator, an Assistant Grand Secretary,
a Grand Marshal, a Grand Standard Bearer, a Grand Sword Bearer, a

253

B.

Members of Grand Lodge shall meet in Communications to conduct
whatever business may properly come before them.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 200.020 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§200.020. NO POLITICAL OR RELIGIOUS INVOLVEMENT.
Grand Lodge and its Constituent Lodges shall not interfere or voice an
opinion with regard to political or religious matters. Masons Members, when they
are assembled in Constituent Lodges or Grand Lodge, may not discuss political or
religious matters. No invocation, benediction or prayer shall be delivered which
would have a sectarian significance.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 200.040 of the California Masonic
Code be amended as marked:
§200.040. NO BUSINESS ACTIVITIES.
A Masonic Lodge is not a business establishment. Therefore, a Masonic
Lodge may not under any circumstance regularly offer goods or services to the
general public. A Masonic Lodge may not under any circumstance provide a forum
which encourages business relations to grow nor which enhances any commercial
advantage of its members. No Mason member of any Masonic Lodge may engage
in any of these activities except in his individual capacity and then only without
the use of the name of the Lodge or reference to his involvement in Masonry.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 403.000 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:

254

Proceedings of the

§403.000. PREREQUISITE TO MEMBERSHIP IN GRAND LODGE.
Each member of Grand Lodge must be a member in good standing of a
chartered and duly constituted Lodge in this Jurisdiction (other than a Research
Lodge or a Historic Lodge). If such membership ceases, membership in Grand
Lodge shall cease.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 403.005 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§403.005. ELECTED LODGE REPRESENTATIVES.
Each chartered and duly constituted Lodge in this Jurisdiction (other
than a Research Lodge, a Historic Lodge or the Grand Master’s Lodge) may elect
a member thereof to represent it at the next Annual or Special Communication
in the event that neither the Master nor either of the Wardens can be present at
such Communication. Such election shall be by ballot at a Stated Meeting or
at a Special Meeting of the Lodge called for that purpose, by a majority of the
members present and voting.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 404.000 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§404.000. PREREQUISITE FOR OFFICERS.
Each officer of Grand Lodge must be a member in good standing of
a Constituent Lodge (other than a Research Lodge or a Historic Lodge). Each
officer, other than the Grand Chaplain, Grand Organist and Assistant Grand
Organist, must also, at the time of his election or appointment, be a Past Master of
this Jurisdiction or a Master or Warden of a chartered and duly constituted Lodge
of this Jurisdiction (other than a Research Lodge, a Historic Lodge or the Grand
Master’s Lodge).
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 404.410 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§404.410. ELECTED OFFICERS.
The Grand Master, Deputy Grand Master, Grand Wardens, Grand
Treasurer, Grand Secretary, and Grand Lecturer shall be elected by written ballot
as the final item of business before the installation of said officers at each Annual
Communication. A majority of the votes cast shall be necessary for an election.
Grand Lodge, by unanimous consent, may permit any designated officer to cast
the ballot for Grand Lodge.

255

Each recommendee for election to any Grand Lodge office shall provide
his biographical sketch to the Grand Secretary no less than two weeks prior to the
start of Annual Communication. Any other member desiring to be nominated for
election as a Grand Lodge officer may provide his biographical sketch to the Grand
Secretary no less than two weeks prior to the start of Annual Communication.
Nominations for election to any Grand Lodge office shall include only the name
and current title of the nominee. At the conclusion of the nomination process for
each elective office, if there are multiple nominees, the Grand Orator shall read
the biographical sketch submitted for each nominee, if received by the Grand
Secretary him at least two weeks prior to the start of Annual Communication,
in the order of their nominations. The biographical sketch of the Junior Grand
Warden shall be read by the Grand Orator whether or not there are multiple
nominees. The Grand Orator shall read only the facts from each biographical
sketch. If the Grand Secretary did not receive a biographical sketch for a nominee
by the required date, the vote shall be taken without reading a biographical sketch
for that nominee.
Each elective officer shall be installed before the close of the Annual
Communication and shall serve until the installation of his successor, subject to
Section 404.510. This installation may be public or private at the option of the
incoming Grand Master.
If an elective officer is unable to be present, due to circumstances beyond
his control, he may be installed by the Grand Master at an appropriate place, with
such ceremony as deemed proper by the Grand Master, as soon as practicable
not to exceed 60 days. If the elective officer is not installed within 60 days, the
office shall be declared vacant and the Grand Master may appoint any member of
Grand Lodge to fill the vacant elective office temporarily or for the remainder of
the Grand Lodge year.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 406.000 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§406.000. COMMITTEE MEMBERSHIP.
Members of committees shall be members of Grand Lodge or Master
Masons who are members in good standing in Constituent Lodges (other than
Research Lodges or Historic Lodges) whose special talents, in the discretion of the
Grand Master, are considered to be desirable or required for the accomplishment
of the mission of the committees. At least seventy percent of the total number of
members on each committee shall be members of Grand Lodge.
If a member has served as chairman of the committee for five consecutive
years, he shall be ineligible for reappointment as chairman of that committee until
the lapse of one year. If a member has served on a committee for nine consecutive
years, including service as chairman, he shall be ineligible for reappointment to
that committee until the lapse of one year.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 407.050 of the California

§407.050. GRAND LODGE BUDGET.
Grand Lodge shall have a budget for each fiscal year as follows:
A.

The Grand Lodge Budget shall be prepared under the direction and
control of the Deputy Grand Master. The Grand Treasurer and the Grand
Lodge Committee on Finance shall consult in the preparation of the
Grand Lodge Budget as requested by the Deputy Grand Master. The
Deputy Grand Master shall be assisted in the preparation of the budget
by such other persons as he may select to assist him;

B.

Each Grand Lodge Budget shall be based upon the per capita sum to be
collected for Master Masons carried on the rolls of each Constituent Lodge
as of the June 30th most immediately preceding the commencement of
the fiscal year covered by such budget;

C.

The proposed Grand Lodge Budget shall be transmitted by the Grand
Secretary to the Masters of the several Lodges, Inspectors and members
of the Committee on Finance at least 30 days prior to the commencement
date of the next Annual Communication;

D.

The proposed Grand Lodge Budget shall be referred to the Committee
on Finance for its review and report to Grand Lodge before the vote is
taken whether to adopt the budget;

E.

The Deputy Grand Master shall present the proposed budget to the
members of Grand Lodge for their approval. The Grand Lodge Budget
shall be adopted by a majority vote;

F.

The Grand Treasurer and the Committee on Finance shall monitor
compliance with the adopted Grand Lodge Budget during the Grand
Lodge year;

§406.005. STANDING COMMITTEES.
The members of standing committees (other than those who serve exofficio) shall be appointed by the newly installed Grand Master at each Annual
Communication before the close thereof. A member ceases to be a standing
committee member by death, removal by the Grand Master (other than those
members who serve ex-officio), resignation, ceasing to be a member of a
Constituent Lodge or suspension or expulsion as a Mason. In the event of any
vacancy on any standing committee other than the Executive Committee or Ritual
Committee, the Grand Master may appoint a successor for the balance of the
current term. All standing committee appointments (other than those who serve
ex-officio) shall expire at the close of the next succeeding Annual Communication.
The following are standing committees of the Grand Lodge: Annual
Communications Activities, Audit, California Freemason, Compensation,
Executive (all of whose members serve ex-officio), Finance, Investments,
Jurisprudence, Lodge Support, Masonic Properties, Legislative Analysis, Ritual
(all of whose members serve ex-officio) and Trial Review.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 409.030 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§409.030. RECOGNITION OF PRINCE HALL GRAND LODGE OF
CALIFORNIA.
Any other provision of this Code to the contrary notwithstanding, this
Grand Lodge recognizes the Most Worshipful Prince Hall Grand Lodge, Free
and Accepted Masons of the States of California and Hawaii, Inc. Incorporated
as having concurrent jurisdiction with this Grand Lodge within the State of
California. This recognition includes the following:
A.

A Mason may have Masonic Communication with any Mason of a
Masonic Lodge which has been chartered by, or holds allegiance to,
the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California, with one exception. While
outside this Jurisdiction, a Mason shall not have Masonic Communication
with any Mason of a Masonic Lodge which has been chartered by, or
holds allegiance to, the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California, unless
the Grand Lodge which we recognize with jurisdic­tion over that state or
territory recognizes the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California.

B.

A Mason may have Masonic Communication with any person legally
present at the tiled meeting of a Masonic Lodge or Masonic Organization
within this Jurisdiction which has been chartered by, or holds allegiance
to, the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California. A Mason may have
Masonic Communication with any person legally present at the tiled
meetings of the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California. During such
a tiled meeting, a Mason may have Masonic Communication with any
person legally present even though such a person is not a Mason of a
Masonic Lodge chartered by or holding allegiance to a Grand Lodge
recognized by the Grand Lodge of California. This exception applies
only during such a tiled meeting and at no other time.

A Mason of a Masonic Lodge chartered by, or holding allegiance to,
the Prince Hall Grand Lodge of California shall not be subject to the disciplinary
jurisdiction of this Grand Lodge.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 409.040 of the
California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§409.040. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS OF FOREIGN JURISDICTIONS.
A Mason member of a Constituent Lodge, when in another Jurisdiction,
may act in accordance with the law, policy and practice of that Jurisdiction and
shall obey and be subject to the Masonic law of the other Jurisdiction and also
to the Masonic law of this Jurisdiction which is consistent with the practice,
policy or law of the other Jurisdiction. A Mason member of a Constituent Lodge
may not do anything in this Jurisdiction in violation of the Masonic law of this
Jurisdiction whether he resides or is in or out of this Jurisdiction.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

Communication, the Lodge shall deliver to the Grand Secretary the Bylaws,

Communication. If Grand Lodge does not order the issuance of a Charter and does
not revive the Dispensation, then the provisions of Section 813.060 of this Code
shall apply as if the Lodge had been dissolved.

the first day of January.
ARTICLE IV
AMENDMENTS
Section 1. Those portions of these Bylaws relating to the day and time of
Stated Meetings and the amount of fees and dues may be amended at any Stated
Meeting by a two‑thirds vote of the members present who are in good standing.
All proposed amendments must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated
Meeting and written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth
the text of the proposed amendment and the date of the Stated Meeting at which
the vote is to be taken. It shall have no effect until approved by the Grand Master.
The Secretary of the Lodge shall note in the minutes of the Lodge the notice
of the proposed amendments when made. When transmitting an amendment for
approval, he shall forward a certificate, under seal, showing that the law has been
complied with and that the amendment has received the required vote.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 804.550 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:

D.

Every member of a Lodge in good standing, when present, must vote
upon a ballot using a ball or a cube;

§804.550. DECISION OF LODGE ON OBJECTION.

E.

The Master should not permit anyone to enter or retire from the Lodge
room during a ballot except for sickness or other imperative reason. For
this purpose, the “Lodge room” does not include the Tiler’s room or
the preparation room. Members and other Masons visitors may enter or
retire between ballots if in the Master’s judgment such will not interfere
with the taking of the subsequent ballot;

F.

When balloting upon two or more applicants, the Master may at his
discretion determine whether a separate ballot shall be taken on each
applicant or whether the entire group shall be balloted upon collectively.
When a collective ballot is used, the Master shall read the names of all
of the applicants included in the collective ballot, with the essential
information about each, as supplied by the application and/or furnished
by the Investigating Committee. A ballot shall then be taken in the usual
manner on the applicants collectively. If no cube appears, each applicant
shall be declared elected. If one or more cubes appear, the Master may
either direct an individual ballot or divide the names of the applicants
into smaller groups. The Lodge shall then proceed to ballot in the usual
manner on each individual or on each group. The Master shall declare
each applicant in a group elected if no cube appears. This procedure shall
continue until an individual ballot has been taken in the usual manner, if
necessary, and all applicants have been balloted upon;

After receiving the report from the Committee appointed to resolve the
objection, the Lodge shall vote by ballot on whether or not the objection is valid
and Masonic. If in the opinion of two‑thirds of the members present, the objection
is not a valid and Masonic one, the Lodge may confer the degree in the same
manner as if no objection had been made, and the Master shall not allow the
same objection to be made a second time. The decision is final and may not be
reconsidered, and no appeal may be taken.
If the objection is found to be valid and Masonic, the contributions and
that part of the fee for the degree or degrees not taken by the applicant shall be
returned to him. The candidate denied advancement shall have the status of one
rejected for the unconferred degrees. His status shall be reported to the Grand
Secretary, and the time interval applying to other rejections of an application must
elapse before a new application may be made for advancement. The application
shall be made on the form approved by Grand Master and shall take the usual
course of investigation and ballot.

§804.845. DUTY TO OBEY NOTICE.
It is the duty of every Mason to comply with a notice if he can do so

Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§805.620. VACANCY IN ELECTED OFFICE.
If an elected office becomes vacant, the vacancy shall be filled by
election and no dispensation shall be required. Until the election and installation
of another Master, the Senior Warden, if available and if not the Junior Warden,
succeeds to the powers and duties of the Master and acts as Master. Until the
election and installation of another Treasurer, the Master shall be the custodian
of all monies, property and other assets of the Lodge that are not entrusted to
Trustees. Until the election and installation of another Secretary, the Master may
appoint a qualified member of the Lodge to act as Secretary.

§806.000. COMMITTEES.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 807.000 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§807.000. STATED MEETINGS.
A Lodge shall hold a Stated Meeting for the transaction of business
once in each calendar month, on the date (other than a Sunday) and at the time
established in its Bylaws. The foregoing notwithstanding, Lodges whose Bylaws
provide for meetings fixed by the phase of the moon shall hold a Stated Meeting
for the transaction of business once in each lunar month, and Mountain Range
Lodge No. 18, Gravel Range Lodge No. 59, Harmony Lodge No. 164, Sierra
Valley Lodge No. 184 and Truckee Lodge No. 200 shall only be required to hold a
Stated Meeting for the transaction of business once in each of 10 calendar months
during the year, as it may provide in its Bylaws.

C.

Quorum. A Lodge shall not be opened, nor shall any work be done

§807.020. ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS APPLICABLE TO MEETINGS.

G.

No Adjourned Meetings. There shall be no adjourned meeting. Each
meeting of a Lodge must be closed when the business proposed for
transaction has been concluded, but in no event later than the close of the
day on which it was opened.

H.

Good Standing Requirement. No member may make a motion, second
a motion, speak on a motion, vote on a motion, recommend anyone for
membership or ballot on membership at a Lodge meeting unless he is
then a member in good standing of that Lodge. He must present a current
dues receipt to the Tiler to demonstrate that he is a member of the Lodge
in good standing or be verified by the Master, Senior Warden, Junior
Warden, Secretary or Assistant Secretary as a member of the Lodge in
good standing. If a member is present who is not in good standing, any
question or action to be decided hereunder by a majority or greater vote
of the members present shall be decided by a majority or greater vote of
the members present who are in good standing.

The Inspector or Grand Master may grant a dispensation to change the
date of a Stated Meeting, as provided Section 405.060 of this Code.
In the event that the Master of a Lodge determines that inclement weather,
including ice, snow, and flood conditions, existing on the day established in the
Bylaws of the Lodge for its Stated Meeting, makes it hazardous for members of
the Lodge to attend the meeting, he may, with the consent of the Inspector of the
district to which the Lodge is assigned, postpone the Stated Meeting to the same
day of the week next following the week scheduled for the Stated Meeting. The
Master shall notify, to the extent possible, all members of the Lodge residing
within fifty miles of the meeting place of the Lodge of the date of the postponed
Stated Meeting.
Should a Stated Meeting be postponed, the business transacted at the
postponed Stated Meeting shall be limited to the reading of the minutes of the last
Stated and subsequent Special Meetings, action thereon, payment of the invoices
of the Lodge, and such other business of an important nature as determined by
the Master to require immediate consideration. No other new business shall
be considered.

B.

Sunday Meetings. No Stated or Special Meetings of a Lodge shall be
held on Sunday except for the annual Installation of Officers or funeral
services. If the Stated Meeting of a lunar Lodge falls on a Sunday, the

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 809.370 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.370. SUSPENSION FOR NON-PAYMENT OF DUES.
If a Mason has not paid his dues during a period of 12 months, the
Secretary shall notify him that he will be suspended for non-payment of dues
unless at the Lodge’s next Stated Meeting either his dues have been paid or
sickness or inability to pay is shown as the cause for the failure to pay. The
notice shall be given either by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage
prepaid, addressed to his last known address, or by actual service of notice, duly
certified by the Tiler. If all dues due and payable have not been paid by the time
of the Lodge’s next Stated Meeting, he shall be declared suspended by the Master,
unless for special reasons shown the Lodge shall remit his dues or grant him
further time for payment. No worthy brother who is unable to pay his dues shall
be suspended for non-payment of dues.
No Mason who has attained the age of 80 years or who has attained an
aggregate number of years in age and years as a Mason in good standing equaling
120 or more shall be suspended for non-payment of dues without a written report
to the Lodge from the Member Retention Committee evidencing when and where
the committee interviewed the delinquent Mason, why the delinquent Mason has
not paid his dues and whether the delinquent Mason has the ability to pay his
dues. A copy of this report shall be provided to the Grand Secretary at least thirty
days before the vote may be taken on the suspension he may be suspended for
non-payment of dues.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 811.030 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§811.030. FRAUDULENT OR ILLEGAL VENTURES.
Neither a Lodge nor a Mason member thereof shall, directly or indirectly,
engage in or give any aid or support to any business, project, venture, promotion,
scheme or plan which is unethical, fraudulent, misleading or illegal.
Neither a Lodge nor a Mason member thereof shall engage in or give
any aid or support to any business, project, scheme, plan, individual or concern
asserted to be Masonic in character or using any term, name or words implying a
connection with Masonry, whenever facts presented to the Grand Master prove to
his satisfaction that:
A.

Any such business, project, scheme or plan is unmasonic, unethical,
fraudulent, or misleading; or

B.

The individual, group or concern in charge of or employed in the
prosecution, promotion, operation or product of any such business,
project, scheme or plan has indulged in unmasonic, unethical, fraudulent,
misleading acts or practices in connection therewith.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 1404.410 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.410. PROCEDURE IF THE ACCUSED FAILS TO PLEAD.
If the Accused fails, within 30 days as required, to file a statement in
writing containing a plea of guilty, not guilty or no contest, the Trial Master shall,
without further notice to the Accused:
A.

Personally make a complete investigation, including, but not limited to,
a review of documents and interviews to gather relevant information as
to guilt or innocence of the Accused and the penalty, if guilty;

B.

Determine whether the charge and specifications are true;

C.

Cause the facts relating thereto to be reduced to writing;

D.

Make a finding as to the guilt or innocence of the Accused; and

E.

If the Trial Master makes a finding of guilty, fix the penalty under Section
1404.620 of this Code. No other penalty may be imposed.

The Trial Master shall prepare a written report of his investigation, the
verdict and the penalty fixed, if any, including the facts upon which he relied
in fixing the penalty. The Trial Master shall sign the written report and provide
a signed copy to the Grand Secretary. The Trial Master shall cause his signed
written report to be made a part of the trial record.

288

Proceedings of the

The Grand Secretary shall notify the Accused of the findings and the
penalty, if any, fixed by the Trial Master, by certified mail, return receipt requested,
postage prepaid, addressed to the Accused’s last known address as shown in the
Grand Lodge’s records. The Grand Secretary shall also notify the Accuser, the
Accused’s Lodge and the Inspector assigned to such Lodge of these results. If the
Accused is a member of more than one Lodge, the Grand Secretary shall provide
notification of these results to every Lodge of which the Accused is a member, as
shown in Grand Lodge’s records, and the Inspector assigned to each such Lodge.
At the next Stated Meeting of each Constituent Lodge receiving the
Grand Secretary’s notification, the Master shall announce the Trial Master’s
findings and the penalty, if any, fixed. The Master shall admonish the members
present that the name of the Accused, any charge or evidence against him, the Trial
Master’s findings and the penalty imposed may not be disclosed, either directly
or indirectly, to any person not otherwise entitled to the same. The Secretary
shall record in the minutes of the meeting the Trial Master’s findings and the
penalty fixed.
If the penalty includes suspension or expulsion, it shall be effective
immediately upon the Grand Secretary’s receipt of the Trial Master’s written
report fixing the penalty. The notice to the Accused shall include an explanation
of his status as a suspended or an expelled Mason.
If the penalty is reprimand, the Trial Master shall summon the Accused, if
a Master Mason, to appear at a Stated Meeting of any Constituent Lodge selected
by the Trial Master of which the Accused is a member. If the Accused is not a
member of a Constituent Lodge, the Trial Master shall summon the Accused to
appear at a Stated Meeting of any Constituent Lodge selected by the Trial Master.
If the penalty is reprimand and the Accused is an Entered Apprentice or a Fellow
Craft, the Trial Master shall summon the Accused to appear at a Special Meeting
of the Accused’s Lodge, if a Constituent Lodge, and if not a Constituent Lodge,
then any Constituent Lodge selected by the Trial Master. The Trial Master or his
designee shall deliver the reprimand.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 1404.525 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.525. DISQUALIFICATION
VACANCIES.

OF

COMMISSIONERS

on questions involving interpretation of this Code and trial procedures.
After sufficient consultation and deliberation, the Trial Master and
Commissioners shall vote by ballot upon each specification, and the
ballots shall have written on them “yes” or “no.” Each vote shall be
recorded. For each specification, two separate votes shall be taken. The
Trial Master and Commissioners shall first vote by “yes” or “no” on the
first question: “Is it more likely than not that the Accused committed
the act or acts described in the specification?” If a majority of the Trial
Master and Commissioners votes “yes”, then the Trial Master and
Commissioners shall proceed to vote by “yes” or “no” on the second
question: “Do the act or acts committed by the Accused and described
in the specification constitute unmasonic conduct under the California
Masonic Code?” If a majority of the Trial Master and Commissioners
votes “yes” on both questions, the Accused is guilty of the specification.
If the Trial Master and Commissioners cannot find the Accused guilty of
the specification, they may delete any part which they do not find against
the Accused, and return a verdict, for that portion of the specification or
charge of which they find the Accused guilty. If the Trial Master and
Commissioners cannot find the Accused guilty of the specification with
deletions, the Accused shall be found not guilty of the specification.

AND

Objections may be made to any Commissioner at or before the Pre-Trial
Conference, and the reasons for objection must be stated at the time thereof. No
person who acted as a witness or Commissioner at a prior trial of the Accused
may act as a Commissioner. The Trial Master shall decide and rule upon the
validity of all objections. One who cannot fairly try the matter may not act as
a Commissioner.
A Commissioner is automatically removed if he fails to attend on the
date appointed by the Trial Master, or if he fails to attend on any adjourned date.
Any vacancy among the Commissioners, because of an objection,
failure to attend, resignation or otherwise, may be filled by the Trial Master with a
disinterested Master Mason in good standing who resides in this Jurisdiction and
has been a member in good standing of a Constituent Lodge for not less than five
years. There shall not at any time be any fewer than two Commissioners, regardless
of the number of Commissioners originally appointed. No Commissioner may
be appointed by the Trial Master from any Lodge of either the Accuser or the
Accused. If a vacancy occurs after the start of the first evidentiary hearing in the
trial, then the vacancy may only be filled by a Master Mason who has been present
during all evidentiary hearings before his appointment or all evidence introduced
before his appointment must be introduced again.

The final vote on each question shall be recorded, giving the number of
votes, both yes and no, upon each question. This record of the findings
at trial shall be signed by the Trial Master and Commissioners and given
to the Trial Master at the end of the deliberations and vote. The Trial
Master shall provide a signed copy of this record to the Grand Secretary.
The Trial Master shall cause the signed report of the findings at trial to
be made a part of the trial record. After the Trial Master has signed this
record, the Commissioners are discharged and shall have no further part
in the proceedings.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 1404.610 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.610. DELIBERATIONS AND VERDICT.

Should the Accused be found guilty of one or more of the specifications,
as originally charged, or as modified by the Trial Master and
Commissioners, the Trial Master shall proceed to set the penalty under
Section 1404.620 of this Code. No other penalty may be imposed. The
Trial Master shall record the penalty fixed. He shall sign the record of
the penalty fixed and provide a signed copy to the Grand Secretary. The
Trial Master shall cause a copy of the signed record of the penalty fixed
to be made a part of the trial record; or

After all testimony has been received in a trial and summations made:
A.

In a trial before a Trial Master sitting with Commissioners, the Trial
Master and Commissioners shall proceed without delay to deliberate
upon the guilt or innocence of the Accused. During their deliberations,
only the Trial Master and Commissioners may be present, and they
alone shall determine the guilt or innocence of the Accused. Only
the Trial Master and those Commissioners who have participated in
every evidentiary hearing during the trial are entitled to participate
in these deliberations and findings. The Trial Master and at least two
Commissioners must participate in the deliberations, regardless of the
number of Commissioners originally appointed. The Commissioners
may consult with the Trial Master, during their deliberations and voting,

291

B.

In a trial before a Trial Master sitting without Commissioners, the Trial
Master shall proceed alone without delay to deliberate upon the verdict
and penalty. The Trial Master alone shall determine the guilt or innocence
of the Accused and shall decide on the penalty. For each specification,
the Trial Master shall answer each of the following two questions:

292

Proceedings of the
“Is it more likely than not that the Accused committed the act or acts
described in the specification?” “Do the act or acts committed by the
Accused and described in the specification constitute unmasonic conduct
under the California Masonic Code?” If the Trial Master has answered
“yes” on both questions, the Accused is guilty of the specification. The
Trial Master may delete any part of a specification which he does not
find against the Accused, and return a verdict, for that portion of the
specification or charge of which he does find the Accused guilty. If the
Trial Master cannot find the Accused guilty of the specification with
deletions, the Accused shall be found not guilty of the specification.
Should the Trial Master find the Accused guilty of one or more of the
specifications, as originally charged, or as modified by him, he shall
proceed to set the penalty under Section 1404.620 of this Code. No
other penalty may be imposed.

This proposal makes a number of minor corrections to the California

adopted legislation have created inconsistencies elsewhere in the Code. Some of
